context: The security team has identified a vulnerability in the ECC key exchange. Four remediations have been proposed. Evaluate whether each one would prevent an attacker from recovering the secret scalar s from the public parameters.

remediations.title: Scale modulus size
remediations.description: Double the composite modulus bit-length from 170 to 340 bits while retaining the identical curve algebraic structure and the same prime selection method (both primes p with p congruent to 3 mod 4, and p+1 being B-smooth for B = 2^18).

remediations.title: Switch to prime-field ECC
remediations.description: Replace the composite modulus with a single prime of equivalent bit-length (170+ bits) and use an elliptic curve whose group order is nearly prime (cofactor h at most 4).

remediations.title: Harden subgroup orders
remediations.description: Retain the composite modulus and the same curve algebraic form, but select primes so that the curve group orders over each prime field each contain a prime factor exceeding 2^128.

remediations.title: Upgrade symmetric layer
remediations.description: Replace AES-256-CBC with XChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption for the symmetric layer, keeping the ECC key exchange parameters entirely unchanged.
